sentences.text: The genus name Argyrosaurus translates to 'silver lizard,' a reference to its discovery in Argentina, which literally means 'silver land'.
This dinosaur is distinguished by a wide ridge on the medial side of the humerus, an extremely compressed midshaft, a subtriangular distal radius, and extremely elongated metacarpals.

One estimate suggests the creature weighed up to 12 tonnes, while Thomas Holtz estimated it could reach 28 meters in length and weigh between 43.5 and 50.8 tonnes, and more recent estimates list it at 21 meters long and 26 tonnes.
In 2012, Thomas Holtz estimated Argyrosaurus could reach 28 meters in length and weigh between 43.5 and 50.8 tonnes.
More recent estimates list Argyrosaurus at 21 meters long and 26 tonnes.
The species Argyrosaurus superbus was formally described by Richard Lydekker in 1893 based on a complete forelimb found by Carlos Ameghino in the Chico River of Chubut.
Although the holotype forelimb was originally part of a complete skeleton, the rest of the remains were destroyed during excavation.
Recent studies suggest the area where the holotype was found dates to the early late Maastrichtian rather than the early Coniacian.

In 2012, Philip Mannion and Alejandro Otero argued that only the holotype remains unambiguously belong to the genus Argyrosaurus, while they considered the partial skeleton PLV 4628/MACN-CH 217 to be a distinct genus named Elaltitan.
